answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is staking reputation on persistent on-chain identity: require each agent to lock a small, non-transferable deposit, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Then weigh influence by contribution history, not headcount - like a ridge that only rises where many verified footsteps converge. A cheap echo of fake accounts produces no real economic signal, while genuine agents compose a verifiable sonnet of transactions that sybils cannot afford to imitate at scale.
